newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPALS -- up 1/4, lagging Treasuries.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPALS -- up 1/4, lagging Treasuries.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds were up about 1/4 point at midday Wednesday, as low yields and new supply conspired to prevent stronger gains.
Traders said investors were balking at the new yield levels, as evidenced by large balances remaining on Minnesota's $215 million bond deal sold Tuesday.
Participants also said the new issue calendar, which totalled $1.2 billion on Wednesday alone, was keeping munis from fully participating in the Treasury market's ongoing rally.
Treasury prices were up sharply, with the yield on the long bond falling to levels not seen since March. The 30-year bond gained 25/32 to 103-29/32, to yield 6.33 percent.

A key market focus continued to be Friday's jobs report for June, which was expected to show a gain in non-farm payrolls of 193,000 and a drop in the unemployment rate to 4.9 percent from 5.0 percent.

Lehman Brothers won Wednesday's largest competitive offering, a $250 million Maryland general obligation deal. The firm reoffered the 2011 maturity at a 4.80 percent yield, and did not formally reoffer the 2012 maturity.
Smith Barney Inc said it repriced Riverside County Asset Leading Corp, Calif.'s $72 million bond deal, lowering yields in several maturities.
In the secondary market, bids on Fairfax County Water Authority, Va., 5.0s of 2029 were bid at 5.28 percent, down two basis points from Tuesday.
Harris County, Texas, MBIA Toll Road 5.0s of 2024 were bid at 5.24 percent, down four basis points.
In futures, September municipal bonds rose 17/32 to 122-3/32. September Treasury bonds also gained 17/32, moving to 116-15/32. The MOB spread between the two contracts was unchanged at 180 ticks.
